llm.summary: This is a disclosed local memory/context pipeline that persistently changes workspace behavior, with privacy caveats but no evidence of exfiltration, deception, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The capabilities match the stated purpose: it installs a context_pipeline bundle, routes user messages, retrieves scoped memory snippets, compresses them into context packs, validates files, and checks memory freshness. The memory-commit workflow can persist user/session information, which is expected for this kind of skill but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The apply flow states that it lays down files and patches AGENTS.md, and runtime instructions say the pipeline becomes default behavior after installation. Some routing and memorization triggers are broad, and the daily-log trigger comment conflicts with ops/briefing caps that enable daily logs by default.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation uses clawhub install plus local Python scripts. The installer copies bundled assets into context_pipeline, the validator reads and hashes files, and the watchdog reads memory logs; no hidden dependency installation, network call, or credential access was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Access is mostly scoped to workspace memory files, context_pipeline, AGENTS.md, and debug/audit run artifacts. That is proportionate to a memory pipeline, but users should treat memory files and daily logs as private context that may be surfaced to the agent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally persists context_pipeline files, AGENTS.md instructions, optional .openclaw context-run artifacts, and memory updates. There is no background worker, privilege escalation, destructive deletion, or credential/session-store use in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only in workspaces where persistent agent memory is desired. Review the changes to AGENTS.md, context_pipeline/router.yml, and your memory directory before relying on it; consider tightening broad route triggers and disabling default daily-log retrieval if your logs contain sensitive information.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed a real policy mismatch: the router comment says daily logs are gated by explicit recency requests, but ops and briefing caps enable daily-log retrieval. This is a privacy/quality caveat rather than evidence of malicious behavior because it remains limited to the documented memory scope.
[SQP-1] expected: The persistent apply phrase is broad, but the artifact does disclose that applying the skill installs files and changes AGENTS.md. This should be treated as an install-time consent and clarity issue, not hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The apply/configuration commands are mutating, but they are the documented installation mechanism and include visible diff/status evidence. A separate confirmation or dry-run would improve user control.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad substring routing in router.yml is confirmed. It can over-select memory sources, including operational context, but routing and retrieval are core to the skill and are capped to named memory paths.
[SQP-1] expected: The memory commit phrases can cause persistent memory updates, but they are documented as the explicit memory workflow. Users should preview what will be stored if sensitive information is involved.
